title: Documentation surfaces — the built-in guide corpus

rules.why: The 28 built-in guide topics are shown by osaurus_help and read as product documentation, so the product name must match the app. The negative lookahead keeps the B-class upstream services (Osaurus Cloud/Router/ID/Identity/Secure/Premium/Connect) untouched per R7; lowercase identifiers, OSAURUS_* env vars, domains and the OsaurusAI HF org are already shielded by the frozen-literal list in brand.json.
The data root moved to ~/.nuo in Phase 2. Guides that still print ~/.osaurus send users to a directory the app no longer writes (the legacy tree stays untouched on disk by design).

The installed helper is `nuo`; `osaurus ui` and friends no longer exist as commands. Matches both the inline form (`osaurus ui`) and the line-start synopsis blocks (`osaurus config export …`). Subcommands stay intact; prose that merely mentions the old name (the frozen Codex profile `codex --profile osaurus`) has no backtick and no line start, so it is out of scope.

`Osaurus` starts with a vowel sound and `Nuo` does not, so the article the rename inherited is wrong: 'an Nuo identity' reads as a typo. Mirrors ui-text's article rule, extended to the backticked `nuo` command form.

rules.pattern: the GitHub releases page or `brew install --cask osaurus`
rules.why: The upstream cask installs the upstream app, not Nuo.app. Until the fork publishes its own cask, the guide must not offer a command that fetches a different product (same reasoning as the README badge rewrite in Phase 5).
The example tells an MCP host which executable to spawn. The installed helper is `nuo`; pointing hosts at the retired name only works while the one-release compatibility symlink exists.
